judgmentCalls: task 2: out-of-FILES: fleet/kata-client.mjs — the task's Context says to "add a `patchMetadata(projectId, uid, body)` beside" the janitor's hub client's `close`, but that client is `makeKataClient` from `fleet/kata-client.mjs`, which already exports a `patchMetadata(projectId, uid, patch, revision)` that sends `If-Match` and no `Idempotency-Key`. A second method of the same name is impossible, and `fleet/tests/test_run_engine_kata_close.mjs:624` pins `Object.keys(makeKataClient(…))` exactly, so a new method name would break a passing sim. I extended the existing one's fourth argument instead: a number/string is still the revision and still sends `If-Match: "rev-<n>"` (test_kata_client.mjs unchanged and green), while `{idempotencyKey}` sends the key and no `If-Match` — the measured shape the task names. The body is `{actor, patch}` either way. This also keeps the death correct under `fleet/launch.mjs:954`, which hands the janitor a client it built rather than letting `openHub` build one — a janitor-local wrapper could not have reached that path.

task 2: plan-defect: the task's Context describes the janitor's hub client as a bespoke ssh-curl seam `openHub` builds whose only write is `close`; it is in fact `makeKataClient({transport: sshTransport(…)})`, which already has a `patchMetadata`. This is a disclosure of how I resolved that, not an unsatisfiable leg — every Proof leg passes.

task 2: out-of-FILES: fleet/kata-client.mjs was modified by the prior commit (281db3a3), outside my declared FILES. Its `patchMetadata(projectId, uid, patch, at)` now accepts `{idempotencyKey}` in place of a numeric revision, so the janitor's death mark can post `…/issues/<uid>/metadata` with `Idempotency-Key: janitor:run-<N>:death` and no `If-Match`, as M3 requires. The change is strictly additive — the numeric-revision If-Match path is unchanged and test_kata_client.mjs plus all three run-engine kata suites still pass — and run-engine.mjs itself is untouched. I kept it rather than re-implementing an ssh-curl POST inside janitor.mjs, which would duplicate the client's internal `mutation` seam.

task 2: plan-defect: the task Context describes the janitor's hub client as "the ssh-curl seam `openHub` builds (~line 599), whose `close` posts to `…/actions/close`" and says to "add a `patchMetadata(projectId, uid, body)` beside it". In the actual code, `openHub` (fleet/janitor.mjs:204) builds `makeKataClient({transport: sshTransport(...), actor: HUB_ACTOR})` from fleet/kata-client.mjs, which already has both `close` and `patchMetadata` — there is no janitor-local seam to add a method to. That is why the idempotency-key affordance landed in kata-client.mjs; the observable behaviour the task specifies (one POST to `…/issues/<run uid>/metadata`, body `{actor:'janitor', patch:{...}}`, that Idempotency-Key, no `actions/close`) is unchanged and is what the exam asserts.

task 1: plan-defect: the Context's knob for M1's third exit is incomplete — `STUB_ENGINE_CODE: '1'` ALONE does not make the page `failed`. The boot downgrades exit 1 WITH a gate receipt to a verdict ('a verdict, not a crash'), and the engine stub writes a receipt by default, so that run ends `done`. A genuinely failed run needs `STUB_ENGINE_CODE: '1', STUB_NO_RECEIPT: '1'` (or a non-1 exit code); the sibling sim's new engine-exit case uses the former and passes. This is pre-existing rig behaviour, not something the implementation can or should change (the `done` path is untouched) — flagged so the exam's engine-exit leg pairs the knob.
